subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: For Windows exec commands containing PowerShell expansion syntax, should OpenClaw preserve the command text and require one-shot explicit approval, or document that direct inline PowerShell variables are unsupported?
rationale: The source path is clear enough to keep the issue open, but the permanent behavior affects command-fidelity expectations and the exec approval security boundary.

options.title: Land One-Shot Expansion Approval After Proof
options.body: Use the open candidate PR direction once live Windows/Gateway proof shows expansion commands do not auto-review, do not allow durable approval, and do not hang.

options.title: Document Script-File Workaround
options.body: Close the behavior as unsupported and document `.ps1`/`-File` as the supported PowerShell-variable path instead of changing approval semantics.

options.title: Design A Broader Raw PowerShell Mode
options.body: Defer the current PR and define a larger explicit PowerShell/raw-command contract before implementation.

recommendation.title: Land One-Shot Expansion Approval After Proof
recommendation.body: Use the open candidate PR direction once live Windows/Gateway proof shows expansion commands do not auto-review, do not allow durable approval, and do not hang.

likelyOwner.reason: The current Windows scanner and approval-boundary history point to steipete as the best available owner for the product/security boundary decision.
